summary: Fiji’s restoration agenda seeks to restore 30% of priority degraded ecosystems and plant 30 million trees, including mangroves, by 2035; mangrove targets rise to 48,000 ha in 2025–2027 and 50,000 ha in 2025–2029, while degraded-area reforestation reaches $1.8 million and $2.8 million. Conservation pledges designate 30% of the EEZ as marine protected areas and manage 100% sustainably by 2030, raise long-term conservation to 18 then 19 forest reserves/parks, and set forest at 63% then 64% of total area, compared with 67.9% mapped in 2022 (12,521 km²). Agriculture commitments include biogas-system targets of 200 and 1,000, 1,500 improved-breed livestock, and support for 100 smallholder farmers by 2035; organic-support recipients rise from 15,000 in 2026 to 25,000 in 2028. By 2035, 50% of agricultural area should be productively and sustainably managed—half of the 5,477 km² mapped as agriculture—and 50% irrigated, while agricultural adoption targets are 10–13%.
